take_homes: An agent only knows what someone wrote down. The first question is therefore who writes the knowledge down, and what that asks of them.
Start with proposal-only agents where the agent drafts and a person decides what leaves. That is something a works council can accept.
A page that a competitor could have written isn't compounding. Citations show whether the agent used our files.

monday.move: Draft the agent for my weekly people-metrics summary, proposal-only, using only non-personal aggregate data. Before anything else, ask the DPO and the works council representative what is allowed.
monday.who: Me, then one HR business partner as the first reader. DPO and works council contact for the data question.
monday.when: Ask Monday morning. Build after I get an answer, probably end of the week.
monday.stop_condition: The DPO or works council says employee data can't go into the tool, or the HR business partner finds the output no more useful than what we do today.
monday.blocker: Employee data in an AI tool needs the works council and the DPO, and I haven't asked yet.

misconception.why: The module never touched roles or headcount, so my question of which roles go is still open. 'It can only use what someone wrote down' made me think about who writes things down, but that is a new question and didn't change what I believed.

one_line: Useful idea that an agent works from files you keep, but it's a tool day and nobody said what it means for the people doing the work.
